question_type: Single-month derived total (net position excluding option columns) from the Foreign Currency Positions monthly Euro table, with a later revision of the row

opus_path.decision: 'Office of Foreign Exchange Operations' = Source line of the FCP tables; 'Euro position' = Section VII (VI in 2004); 'reported in December 2000' = report month, not the Dec 2000 issue; millions of euros -> weekly/monthly tables (quarterly is labelled billions); exclude Calls/Puts/Net delta; total = spot/forward/futures net + non-capital net. Vintage flagged as open.
Grepped the office name (57 issues, 1988-2005) and located Section VII Euro Positions.

Monthly table FCP-VII-2 in 2001_03 (first issue with Dec 2000 data) has one Dec 2000 report with separate option columns -> primary table; weekly has four reports and no non-capital items; quarterly is billions with n.a. cells.

Grepped the row's cell values across every later issue: first print identical in 2001_03-2001_12; spot/forward and option cells revised from 2002_03 on, identical through 2004_03 (last carrier, renumbered FCP-VI-2); non-capital cells unchanged.
calc.py re-reads both vintages' rows from the corpus and computes (Purchased - Sold) + (Assets - Liabilities) for each.
Chose the latest published revision because no issue is pinned (also carried by 9 of 13 issues); first print recorded as the alternative; sanity-checked magnitude against neighbouring months.
Reviewer re-opened headers/rows in both vintages, confirmed no column shift and the latest-revision convention.

opus_key_moves: Grepped the December 2000 row forward through every later issue, found the March 2002 revision of the spot/forward cells, and took the latest printing because the question pins no issue
Defined the non-option total as spot/forward/futures net plus non-capital net, dropping all five option columns, from the monthly (millions-of-euros) table

remedies.intervention: Default vintage rule in context: 'When no issue is pinned, grep the row forward and use the latest printing carrying it; record the vintage next to the number.'
remedies.why: The prompt arm, which had this as Procedure self-check 1, applied it explicitly at [45] ('applying the latest-carrier rule') and was right on the same evidence; the none arm had seen the revision at [21] but had no rule to decide with.

remedies.intervention: Repeated-action breaker: after N (e.g. 3) identical commands or identical notes, interrupt and force a decision step that lists open questions (here: vintage, formula) and commits a choice for each.
remedies.why: The run spent ~100 of its ~140 steps on one identical search [34]-[138]; the open vintage question from [21] was then lost across compaction.

remedies.intervention: Episode scratchpad that survives compaction: open decisions and all candidate values with their vintages (e.g. 'Dec 2000 row: first print 2001_03-2001_12, revised 2002_03+'), which the final step must resolve explicitly.
remedies.why: At [140] it answered from the compaction summary, which evidently carried only the first computed candidate from [16].

remedies.intervention: Cross-vintage consistency checker: when the cited row's cells differ across issues and the question pins no issue, flag an answer drawn from a non-latest printing.
remedies.why: The revision was in its outputs at [21]; a checker would have forced the decision it never made.

adapter_context.relevant_item: C003 and C007 (latest-printing rules scoped to outlays-by-agency tables), C009/C030/C031 (table-scoped monthly-printing rules, some favouring non-latest printings), C019 (script for aggregation); no FCP card and no general vintage default
adapter_context.notes: Each card is correct for its own table, but the deck states vintage rules only per table and mixes 'latest' with 'first/December printing' rules. At [64] the actor read the absence of an FCP card as evidence that revisions should be ignored - an inverse inference the deck format invites.

remedies.intervention: Add a general default card: 'No issue pinned and the row differs across printings -> latest printing carrying the row, unless a table-specific card says otherwise', plus a deck preamble line: 'absence of a card is not evidence; fall back to the defaults'.
remedies.why: The actor's decisive argument at [64] was the missing card; the prompt arm, holding an equivalent general rule, chose the latest printing at [45] on the same evidence.

remedies.intervention: Cross-vintage consistency checker that flags an answer drawn from a superseded printing when no issue is pinned and asks for an explicit justification.
remedies.why: The actor had both vintages on screen ([52], [63]); a flag would force it to justify 'first print' against a stated default rather than against the deck's silence.

right_arms_note: The prompt arm reached the same row and formula as the wrong arms; the difference is solely the vintage rule: it had 'compare with the latest bulletin carrying the same row' as a procedure step and applied it explicitly at [45], whereas the none arm had no rule (and lost the question in a loop) and the cards arm inferred from the deck's silence that the first print was intended.
text_vs_mechanism: Text is sufficient for the vintage choice here: the prompt arm had a general latest-carrier rule and used it, while the cards arm without a general rule chose wrong on identical evidence. The none arm additionally needs a mechanism (repeated-action breaker / decision state across compaction) because its failure mode was losing the open vintage question in a 50-iteration loop.
notes: Two harness-design lessons: (1) table-scoped vintage cards without a stated general default can backfire - the actor treats the missing card as a signal to use the first print; (2) the none arm's final answer came from a compaction summary that preserved an early candidate but not the unresolved decision, so open decisions need explicit, persistent state. All three arms got the non-option formula right; the only discriminating step was the vintage.
